title: hotfix(slo): fix premature circuit-breaker tripping during regional failover and adjust load-shedding thresholds
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: During a recent regional failover exercise we observed an increase in internal retry traffic that caused the SLO enforcement circuit-breaker to trip prematurely for a subset of endpoints. That triggered aggressive load-shedding which exacerbated customer-visible errors. This PR contains a focused hotfix to avoid premature CB tripping during failover windows and to make load-shedding behavior more conservative when regional retries are detected.

What this change does: 1) Adjusts the circuit-breaker sliding window calculation to exclude 'failover-internal' traffic (requests tagged by the failover manager). 2) Caps consecutive backoff increments applied by the enforcer when failover is active to prevent runaway shedding. 3) Adds a short cooldown grace period after a region-failover event before SLO-based shedding can escalate. 4) Adds metrics to track shedding_ratio, failover_tagged_traffic, and cooldown_state to make behavior observable. 5) Adds unit and integration tests for regional failover + SLO interactions and a canary flag to gate rollout.

Why: This is a hotfix — the change minimizes behavioral surface area while addressing an urgent reliability regression observed in the incident (see linked ticket ENG-2345). It preserves existing SLO enforcement semantics for normal traffic and introduces observability so we can tune thresholds post-deployment.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests and an integration harness that simulates multi-region failover were added. CI showed an intermittent lint failure on first run and passed after the formatting fix. We'll deploy as a canary to dedicated-canary region followed by global rollout when metrics look stable.

Checklist: - [x] Add code change to runtime SLO enforcer - [x] Add tagged-exclusion logic in failover manager - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics + dashboard PR queued - [x] Canary rollout plan documented (ops runbook updated)

Related: Linear ENG-2345, SRE-112. Incident reference: SUP-78.
commits: fix(slo): ignore failover-internal tagged traffic in sliding-window calculation
fix(slo): cap backoff increments when failover active
feat(metrics): emit shedding_ratio and failover_tagged_traffic counters
test(slo): add integration test for regional-failover + shedding
review_comments: Jordan Li (reviewer): Can we avoid making the sliding window calculation expensive? Suggest using tag-aggregates instead of per-request filter.
Asha Kapoor (author): Switched to using aggregated counters on the failover manager side; we only lookup tags at insertion time. Window rollup remains O(1).
Priya Nair (reviewer): Are there any cases where legitimate client traffic is incorrectly tagged? We should ensure the tagging logic is strictly internal.
Asha Kapoor (author): Tagging is done inside server/failover_manager.go and is guarded by internal-only header and K8s annotation; added an assertion in tests to prevent escapes.
Max Turner (approver): Verified unit + integration tests locally, CI passed on rerun. Approving to merge as hotfix.
release_notes: Patch: Prevent premature SLO circuit-breaker tripping during regional failover. Adds metrics for shedding behavior and a cooldown window after failover events.
merge_details: Merged via squash by Max Turner on 2025-02-15. Rollout: canary deployed to dedicated-canary region; global rollout gated on shedding_ratio < 0.05 and no customer errors for 30m.
notes_for_ops: Ops: watch telemetry.shedding_ratio and telemetry.failover_tagged_traffic. The canary flag is ops.feature.slo_failover_guard. If shedding_ratio > 0.1 post-canary, rollback immediately and open SRE oncall.
